descriptionChirho: The personal name Tahath (תַּחַת), referring to individuals in Israelite genealogies—an Ephraimite and a Kohathite Levite (1 Chronicles 6-7). Translations use personal name transliterations: Spanish 'Tájat/Tajat,' Arabic 'تَحَت,' Hindi 'तहत,' Korean '다핫,' Swahili 'Tahathi.' The conjunctive and bare forms ('and Tahath' / 'Tahath') are purely grammatical variation for the same personal referent in genealogical lists.

The place name Tahath (תַּחַת), a wilderness station in the Israelite desert itinerary (Numbers 33:26-27). Distinguished by locative prepositions: English 'in Tahath / from Tahath,' Spanish 'en Tahat / de Tahat,' Hindi 'तहत से / तहत में' (from Tahath / in Tahath), Arabic 'مِنْ تَاحَتَ / فِي تَاحَتَ' (from/in Tahath), Korean '타하에서 / 타하에' (from/at Tahath), Swahili 'kutoka Tahathi / katika Tahathi' (from/in Tahath). The spatial prepositions confirm a geographic location rather than a person.
